item.title: Political party leaders worldwide laud 5th plenary session of 20th CPC Central Committee
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-01
BEIJING, Oct. 31 (Xinhua) -- Leaders of political parties around the world have extended congratulations on the successful convening of the fifth plenary session of the 20th Central Committee of the Communist Party of China (CPC). They spoke highly of the CPC's experience and achievements in persistently advancing full and rigorous Party self-governance, and highly appreciated the important insights that Xi Jinping Thought on Party Building offers for the development of political parties around the world. Abhisit Vejjajiva, leader of Thailand's Democrat Party and former Thai prime minister, said that the CPC has accurately grasped major trends in global development and responded to the fundamental demands of the people. The CPC's governance practices and valuable experience offer valuable lessons and are worthy of serious reflection by other political parties, he said. Madhav Kumar Nepal, co-coordinator of the Nepali Communist Party and former Nepali prime minister, said Xi Jinping Thought on Party Building has answered questions that all political parties must confront but few have seriously addressed. Only by consistently attaching great importance to party building and having the courage to renew itself can a political party lead a country toward lasting peace and stability, he said. Luther Tarpeh, national chairman of the Unity Party of Liberia, said the CPC's successful governance model has paved the way for national rejuvenation with sustainable development, offering valuable lessons for the Global South countries. Sophia Shaningwa, secretary general of Namibia's South West Africa People's Organization (SWAPO) party, said that Xi Jinping, general secretary of the CPC Central Committee, has offered an effective solution to address the issue of party governance. SWAPO is willing to enhance exchanges and mutual learning with the CPC, and systematically study Xi Jinping Thought on Party Building, she said. Asha-Rose Migiro, secretary-general of Tanzania's Chama Cha Mapinduzi party, said that this meeting will consolidate the institutional foundation for Chinese modernization and the successful implementation of the 15th Five-Year Plan for National Economic and Social Development. Richard Todwong, secretary-general of Uganda's National Resistance Movement, said the CPC's efforts to strengthen party building have provided strong support for realizing Chinese modernization while offering a valuable model for developing countries, including those in Africa, to enhance their governance capacity. Dmitry Novikov, deputy chairman of the Central Committee of the Communist Party of the Russian Federation and first deputy chairman of the State Duma Committee on International Affairs, said what makes the CPC great is its ability to engage in self-reflection, face problems head-on and take action to address them, which ensures that power is exercised to serve the people rather than private interests and that the party maintains vitality and dynamism. In doing so, the CPC has set an example for political parties in other countries, he said. ■

item.title: A journey without pause: how a century-old political party governs itself
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-31
BEIJING, Oct. 31 (Xinhua) -- How does a large ruling party that has long enjoyed the people's support keep moving forward without being lulled by its own success? For the Communist Party of China (CPC), one key to doing so is to stay vigilant and never lose sight of potential risks that come with long-term governance. Faced with the dangers of complacency, inadequate competence, estrangement from the people and corruption, the Party has chosen to confront them head-on. At the just-concluded fifth plenary session of its 20th Central Committee, the CPC reaffirmed its commitment to persevering with full and rigorous Party self-governance. The session took stock of what has been achieved and set out the fundamental task, guiding principles and plans needed to sustain that effort. NOT A PASSING GUST In 2014, when the term "full and rigorous Party self-governance" was first introduced, skeptics asked whether it would be a passing gust. Time has answered. The campaign has neither stopped nor softened. The numbers show the scale of that sustained effort. From January to September 2026, disciplinary inspection and supervision organs across the country opened 800,000 cases and disciplined 680,000 people -- both figures well above the totals for the whole of 2014. These increases require context. Broader oversight and stronger enforcement, aided by big data and other information technologies, have helped uncover more violations. The figures also point to an ongoing task: addressing corruption that has already taken root while preventing new abuses. This is no time to let up. Looking at history, the pattern is evident. Attention to the Party's self-governance has never been an improvised matter. As early as 1926, just five years after the Party's founding, its Central Committee issued its first document aimed at combating corruption. In recent decades, nearly every Central Committee of the Party has convened a dedicated plenary session on Party building. The emphasis has shifted with changing circumstances, but the issue remains a priority on the core political agenda of the Party, which now has more than 101 million members. WHY PARTY SELF-GOVERNANCE MATTERS This year marks the start of the 15th Five-Year Plan (2026-2030) period, a critical stretch for advancing Chinese modernization. Next year, the Party will hold its pivotal 21st National Congress, a highly important meeting and an event of great political significance for both the Party and the country. At this juncture, emphasizing the importance of persevering with full and rigorous Party self-governance is particularly significant for the CPC, whose capacity to lead bears directly on whether Chinese modernization can ultimately succeed. Much remains to be done: cultivating high-caliber officials, building a well-knit organizational system characterized by cross-level alignment and effective implementation, taking firm and coordinated action against corruption, and refining Party and state oversight systems. The implications extend beyond China. As a major contributor to and stabilizer of global economic growth, China offers broad market prospects, stable policy expectations and a sound security environment as it advances Chinese modernization. Through targeted oversight, disciplinary inspection and supervision organs are helping ensure certainty in development and provide strong guarantees for economic and social progress. By persevering with full and rigorous Party self-governance, and combining Party self-supervision with supervision by the people, the CPC has offered the world new experience in supervising and constraining the exercise of power within a political party. ■

item.title: Economic Watch: China's manufacturing PMI softens, high-tech sector maintains expansion
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-31
BEIJING, Oct. 31 (Xinhua) -- China's manufacturing activity moderated in October while high-tech industries continued to expand, as the country pressed ahead with policy efforts to shore up domestic demand, stabilize investment and sustain economic growth. The manufacturing purchasing managers' index (PMI) came in at 49.3 in October, down 0.8 percentage points from the previous month, according to the National Bureau of Statistics (NBS). Huo Lihui, a chief statistician with the NBS, attributed the retreat to some demand being brought forward ahead of the National Day holiday earlier this month and a complex international environment. The production sub-index stood at 49.8, down 1.9 points from September, while the new orders sub-index fell 1.1 points to 49.4, as both supply and demand moderated during the month. The PMI for high-tech manufacturing stood at 51.3, while that for equipment manufacturing came in at 50.6, both remaining above the 50-point threshold that separates expansion from contraction. The figures indicate that emerging industries continued to sustain growth momentum, supported by the ongoing development of new quality productive forces, Huo noted. Manufacturing activity in several advanced industries remained robust. Both the production and new orders sub-indexes for railway, shipbuilding and aerospace equipment manufacturing, as well as computer, communications and electronic equipment manufacturing, stood at 53 or above, pointing to relatively strong supply and demand in these sectors. Large manufacturers continued to report expansion, with their PMI standing at 50.2, despite a slight decline of 0.4 points from the previous month. Meanwhile, the PMI readings for medium-sized and small enterprises came in at 48.4 and 47.5, respectively. On the price front, both major raw material purchasing prices and factory-gate prices remained in expansionary territory, although their growth moderated. The purchasing price sub-index stood at 56.8, down 4 points from September, while the factory-gate price sub-index eased 2.3 points to 51.7, partly reflecting recent declines in the prices of certain nonferrous metals and other commodities. The latest data came as China's economy expanded 4.5 percent year on year in the third quarter, up from 4.3 percent in the second quarter. In the first three quarters, China's economy grew 4.6 percent, in line with the country's annual growth target. With a relatively low comparison base in the final quarter of last year and the effects of existing and additional policy measures continuing to unfold, economic growth could reach 4.6 to 4.7 percent in the fourth quarter, according to Wen Bin, chief economist at China Minsheng Bank. On the monetary front, the People's Bank of China announced that it would complete the transition to an overnight policy rate framework starting Nov. 2, making the overnight reverse repo rate the main policy rate. The central bank has also introduced a liquidity support mechanism for large-scale redemptions at non-bank financial institutions, aimed at containing systemic risks arising from potential feedback loops between investor withdrawals and bond market sell-offs. Meanwhile, investment support is moving into the implementation stage. China had fully deployed 800 billion yuan (about 119 billion U.S. dollars) through new policy-based financial instruments by Oct. 28, with the funds directed toward project capital in areas including artificial intelligence, the digital economy, green development and consumption-related infrastructure. To boost domestic demand, the National Development and Reform Commission is working on a domestic demand expansion strategy for the 2026-2030 period, which puts more focus on public services, direct support for consumers and combines investment in physical assets with investment in human assets. Taken together, recent policy measures reflect China's continued efforts to balance growth stabilization with improvements in economic quality and efficiency, with the focus shifting from expanding funding and introducing new support tools toward improving policy transmission, strengthening institutional frameworks and enhancing economic resilience, Wen noted. ■

item.title: CPC advances Party self-governance with resolute anti-graft efforts
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-31
BEIJING, Oct. 30 (Xinhua) -- The Communist Party of China (CPC) remains resolute in its fight against corruption as part of broader efforts to advance full and rigorous Party self-governance, according to Party officials. At a plenum that concluded Thursday, the CPC Central Committee adopted a resolution on persevering with full and rigorous Party self-governance, stressing the need to maintain a tough stance against corruption and strengthen checks on and oversight over the exercise of power. The Fifth Plenary Session of the 20th CPC Central Committee also called for fortifying the cultural-ethical foundations for championing integrity and disdaining graft, and enhancing coordinated efforts to ensure that officials do not have the audacity, opportunity, or desire to commit corruption. "The anti-graft fight remains a grave and complex challenge, and much remains to be done to eliminate the conditions and fertile ground that give rise to corruption," senior anti-graft official Zhang Fuhai said on Friday at a press conference held by the CPC Central Committee on the guiding principles from the plenum. Since 2012, discipline inspection and supervisory organs across the country have filed 8.105 million cases and punished 7.922 million people, including 963 officials registered with and supervised by the CPC Central Committee, said Zhang, deputy secretary of the CPC Central Commission for Discipline Inspection and deputy head of the National Commission of Supervision. China has over the years launched an unprecedented anti-graft campaign that has reached every level of the Party and government, netting both high-ranking "tigers" and lower-level "flies." Some of the most senior officials -- including former members of the Political Bureau and its Standing Committee, senior military officials, and retirees who left their leading positions years ago -- have been brought to justice. The campaign has continued unabated. In 2025 alone, 115 officials at ministerial level or above were placed under investigation, while 627,000 people were disciplined in cases involving misconduct and graft that affect the people's immediate interests. The same year, China also opened investigations into more than 500 cases of cross-border corruption. It was noted at the plenum this week that the Party must steadfastly follow a distinctive Chinese path of anti-graft and strengthen the Party Central Committee's centralized, unified leadership over anti-corruption work. "We must take systematic steps to address both symptoms and root causes of corruption and adopt a holistic approach that combines severe punishment, targeted remedy, and effective prevention, carrying this fight through to the end," said a communique issued after the plenary session. Zhang said anti-graft authorities will, in line with the arrangements made at the plenum, resolutely win the battle against corruption. "This is a battle that we cannot afford to lose and must never lose." The plenum pledged to take targeted, well-designed measures to select and appoint officials, inspire them to foster and act on the correct view of performance, and enhance their competence in fulfilling duties and breaking new ground. Huang Jianfa, deputy head of the Organization Department of the CPC Central Committee, said at the press conference that strict discipline is not intended to stifle initiative or constrain officials' actions. "Rather, it seeks to set clear direction, enforce rules, promote sound conduct and guard against corruption, fostering a clean political environment and enabling officials to take initiative in their work," he said. The resolution stresses that everyone is equal before the rules, no one enjoys privileges and no exceptions are allowed in their enforcement, said Xie Chuntao, vice president of the Party School of the CPC Central Committee. It also calls for enforcement and oversight to be integrated into every stage of the work of Party organizations, members and officials, ensuring that institutional rules remain authoritative at all times and effective at every level, Xie said at the press conference. FULL, RIGOROUS PARTY SELF-GOVERNANCE The plenum made systematic plans for persevering with full and rigorous Party self-governance. Key priorities include strengthening the Party spirit, improving conduct and tightening discipline, taking firm and coordinated action against corruption, running the Party with systems and regulations, and refining Party and state oversight systems. With over 100 million members, the Party has attached great importance to its own building since it was founded in 1921, said Liu Haixing, a member of the CPC Central Committee and head of the International Department of the CPC Central Committee. For 105 years, he added, Party members have treated Party building as a great project, pressing ahead one generation after another -- forging and tempering the Party into the great, glorious and correct CPC that stands today. "The Party demonstrates the strong vitality of Marxism," he said. As profound changes unseen in a century gather pace across the world, political parties around the globe are confronting a stream of new issues and challenges. "Many political parties are turning their eyes to us in the hope of finding paths and solutions for reference," said Liu. That attention, he noted, attests to the valuable experience the CPC has accumulated during the periods of revolution, development and reform -- experience that progressive forces around the world can draw on. Wu Hansheng, head of the Society Work Department of the CPC Central Committee, underscored the importance of Party building in emerging sectors. Wu's department will work to expand the coverage of Party organizations in these sectors, strengthen Party building and improve services and management for people in new forms of employment. Built on internet platforms, new forms of employment now engage some 84 million workers nationwide, including couriers, ride-hailing drivers and e-commerce workers. Zhong Baijun, party chief of Xijidang Village in Lianyungang City in east China's Jiangsu Province, who attended the plenum as a non-voting participant, said that for communities like the one he leads, the latest arrangements from the meeting mean power at the micro level must be kept in check, affairs handled fairly, and petty graft close to the people rooted out. The aim, he said, is to win public trust with integrity and clean governance. "Weeds don't stop growing just because you've pulled them once," said Zhong, adding that the same goes for the Party's full and rigorous self-governance.■

item.title: Xinhua Headlines: Overseas observers say CPC plenum shows firm resolve in full and rigorous Party self-governance
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-31
BEIJING, Oct. 31 (Xinhua) -- The fifth plenary session of the 20th Communist Party of China (CPC) Central Committee concluded Thursday in Beijing after adopting a resolution on persevering with full and rigorous Party self-governance. Xi Jinping, general secretary of the CPC Central Committee, delivered an important address at the session. The plenum made systematic plans for persevering with full and rigorous Party self-governance, demonstrating the Party's resolve to strengthen its governing capacity, maintain its advanced nature and integrity, and keep close ties with the people, overseas political analysts have said. They commended the Party's sustained efforts to improve governance and combat corruption, noting that the measures would help translate long-term development goals into effective action, consolidate public trust and provide useful insights for other countries seeking stronger institutions and better public services. STRENGTHENING CAPACITY TO DELIVER The session stressed that strict management of officials is the key to full and rigorous Party self-governance. It called for implementing the Party's organizational line for the new era and applying stringent standards to the education, cultivation, selection, appointment, management, and oversight of officials. It also emphasized that Party organizations at all levels play the principal role in exercising full and rigorous Party self-governance, calling for systematically advancing their development at all levels and in all sectors to strengthen their political and organizational functions. For Lyazid Benhami, an expert on China-France relations, full and rigorous Party self-governance helps improve policy consistency, clarify officials' responsibilities and strengthen coordination across different levels of decision-making, all of which are particularly important in a country as large and diverse as China. For China, continuity in major strategic directions helps advance projects that require substantial investment and a long time to complete, he said. Combining that continuity with regular assessments of implementation enables the Party to listen to the public and adjust policies when necessary, Benhami added. Ling Tek Soon, senior lecturer at the Institute of China Studies of the University of Malaya, said the CPC's efforts to address its own problems and combat corruption reflect a long-term vision for governance. By continually improving the overall quality of its officials, the Party also creates room for fresh talent and ideas, he added. Joseph Mutaboba, a former Rwandan diplomat, highlighted the importance of connecting leadership, institutional responsibility and implementation. "Effective governance begins with the quality, integrity and accountability of public officials," he said. Merit-based recruitment, continuous professional development, performance evaluation, and transparent accountability mechanisms are essential for strengthening public institutions, Mutaboba added. BUILDING INTEGRITY, PUBLIC TRUST The CPC has outlined four areas of focus for steadfastly following a distinctive Chinese path to combating corruption, including maintaining a tough stance against corruption, strengthening checks on and oversight over the exercise of power, fortifying the cultural-ethical foundations for championing integrity and disdaining corruption, and enhancing coordinated efforts to prevent corruption by rooting out audacity, opportunity and desire. Eduardo Regalado, a researcher at Cuba's International Policy Research Center, said the approach addresses different causes of corruption: deterrence raises the cost of wrongdoing, institutional safeguards close loopholes, and education makes integrity an internal commitment. He also viewed the central Party leadership's eight-point decision on improving work conduct as an institutional means of curbing undesirable practices and maintaining close ties with the people. "Strengthening Party regulations and institutions turns political will into stable, predictable and binding rules and procedures," Regalado said, adding that this helps make full and rigorous Party self-governance sustainable and consistent with the modernization of national governance. Koh King Kee, president of the Center for New Inclusive Asia, a Malaysian think tank, said the anti-corruption campaign had sent a clear message that no area or individual was exempt from scrutiny. Effective supervision of power, sound institutions and education must advance together so that people experience fairness and justice in their daily lives, Koh said. Alberto Moreno, president of the Communist Party of Peru (Red Fatherland), linked the Party's long-term governing capacity to its ability to prevent corruption, bureaucracy and privilege from weakening its relationship with the people. "The CPC draws its strength from the people and always serves the people," he said. Institutional restraints and ideological education are inseparable, Moreno added, stressing the importance of combining discipline with officials' morality and commitment to public service. SHARING EXPERIENCE The endeavors to advance full and rigorous Party self-governance in the new era have broken new ground in the self-reform of the century-old Party and brought about historic achievements and transformations in the cause of the Party and the country, according to a communique issued following the plenum on Thursday. Such progress in self-reform has drawn praise from observers who see the ability to learn and adapt as essential to a governing party's long-term vitality. Peter Hediger, a Swiss sinologist, said the CPC's experience demonstrates an ongoing process of adapting Marxism to the Chinese context and the needs of the times. "It is the dynamic nature of the CPC which has enabled pragmatic approaches to various political, social, and economic problems," Hediger said. Winston Alarcon, general secretary of the Communist Party of Ecuador, said Xi Jinping Thought on Party Building draws on Marxist theory while responding to China's national conditions, providing guidance for Party development and the country's modernization. The concepts of full and rigorous Party self-governance and self-reform have enriched Marxist thinking on party building, he said. For Latin American societies, an important lesson is the need to study their own history and culture, confront new challenges and develop theories grounded in experience, Alarcon added. Countries should explore independent development paths suited to their circumstances, he noted. Benhami likewise emphasized the wider relevance of combining strategic continuity with self-improvement. Countries with different histories and institutions can draw on that experience as they seek more accountable and effective governance to ensure that public resources serve the public interest and the benefits of development reach the people, he said. ■

item.title: Xi meets president of Swiss Confederation, calling for more certainty for China-Europe economic, trade cooperation
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-30
Chinese President Xi Jinping meets with President of the Swiss Confederation Guy Parmelin, who is paying a working visit to China, at the Great Hall of the People in Beijing, capital of China, Oct. 30, 2026. (Xinhua/Li Xiang) BEIJING, Oct. 30 (Xinhua) -- Chinese President Xi Jinping met with President of the Swiss Confederation Guy Parmelin in Beijing on Friday, calling on both countries to inject confidence and more certainty into China-Europe economic and trade cooperation as well as into the global economic development. Noting Switzerland is an important partner of China in Europe, Xi said Swiss cooperation with China has always been at the forefront among European countries. He added that free trade cooperation has become the brightest highlight of China-Switzerland relations, which fully demonstrates the political courage and responsibility of the two countries in adhering to open cooperation, and highlights the unique leading role of both sides in promoting the building of an open world economy. China is willing to work with Switzerland to uphold openness, strengthen cooperation, promote a universally beneficial and inclusive economic globalization, and jointly inject confidence and more certainty into the economic and trade cooperation between China and European countries, as well as into the global economic development, Xi said. Since the establishment of diplomatic ties, China and Switzerland have continuously translated the China-Switzerland cooperation spirit, featuring equality, innovation and win-win results, into pragmatic outcomes, setting a model for interactions between countries of different sizes and with different social systems, Xi pointed out. He said the two sides should respect each other, treat each other as equals, and comprehensively enhance exchanges and policy alignment at different levels. Noting that China is accelerating the development of new quality productive forces and steadily expanding institutional opening up, Xi said the country is ready to turn its market into a market for the world and a shared market for all. Both sides should adhere to mutual benefit and win-win results, strengthen innovation cooperation and focus on fostering cooperation in emerging industries, including digital economy, green energy storage and artificial intelligence, he added. Xi expressed hope that Switzerland would leverage its unique influence to actively promote balanced and stable development of trade between China and European countries. As China and Switzerland share similar positions and concepts in supporting multilateralism, Xi said both sides should deepen multilateral coordination and mutual support, firmly uphold the international system with the United Nations at its core and the international order based on international law, reform and improve the global governance system, and advance the building of a community with a shared future for humanity. Parmelin said that since the establishment of diplomatic relations, Switzerland and China have always respected each other, maintained close high-level exchanges, and achieved fruitful cooperation results in many fields such as trade and investment, scientific research and innovation, and employment. Noting that this year marks the 10th anniversary of the establishment of Switzerland-China innovative strategic partnership, Parmelin said that the two sides have successfully completed negotiations on signing a protocol on upgrading free trade agreement in a short period of time with high quality, demonstrating a high level of mutual trust between the two sides, which will inject new impetus into bilateral relations. Switzerland firmly adheres to the one-China policy and looks forward to strengthening dialogue and exchanges with China, upholding mutually beneficial cooperation, and promoting greater development in cooperation in various fields, he said. The Swiss side attaches great importance to the positive role played by China in international affairs and is willing to closely coordinate with China, adhere to multilateralism, safeguard free trade, and contribute to world development, prosperity, peace and stability, Parmelin added. After their meeting, the two leaders witnessed the signing of the protocol on upgrading free trade agreement and multiple cooperation documents in areas like scientific research, employment and the media. ■ Chinese President Xi Jinping meets with President of the Swiss Confederation Guy Parmelin, who is paying a working visit to China, at the Great Hall of the People in Beijing, capital of China, Oct. 30, 2026. (Xinhua/Ding Lin)

item.title: Xi holds talks with German president, calls for opening new chapter in all-round strategic partnership
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-30
Chinese President Xi Jinping and his wife Peng Liyuan pose for a group photo with German President Frank-Walter Steinmeier and his wife Elke Budenbender prior to the talks between Xi and Steinmeier at the Great Hall of the People in Beijing, capital of China, Oct. 30, 2026. Xi held talks with Steinmeier, who is on a state visit to China, in Beijing on Friday. (Xinhua/Shen Hong) BEIJING, Oct. 30 (Xinhua) -- Chinese President Xi Jinping held talks with German President Frank-Walter Steinmeier in Beijing on Friday, saying China is ready to work with Germany to open a new chapter in China-Germany all-round strategic partnership and promote the building of a more just and equitable global governance system. Xi said as the world's second and third largest economies, China and Germany bear significant responsibilities for the development of China-EU relations and the stable growth of the world economy. Xi called on both sides to enhance communication and collaboration, create a new model of cooperation featuring equality, mutual benefit and strategic stability, and send out positive signals to the world of choosing openness over isolation and cooperation over confrontation. China's policy toward Germany is consistent, stable and predictable, and China is happy to see Germany play a greater role in European and international affairs, Xi said, noting that China has attached great importance to Germany's status as a major country and always supported its reunification and development. Xi expressed hope that Germany will view China's development and its cooperation with China with an open and positive attitude, uphold a rational, pragmatic and friendly policy toward China, and adhere to mutual respect and equal treatment, which is a valuable piece of experience for the sustained and sound development of China-Germany relations. Noting that Germany is a representative of advanced manufacturing and high-quality products, while China is advancing its modernization through high-quality development, Xi said the two sides have compatible development strategies and broad space for cooperation. Xi said China welcomes enterprises from Germany and other countries to deepen their presence in China and share the benefit of its supersized market. It is hoped that the German side will provide a fair, transparent and non-discriminatory business environment for Chinese enterprises operating in Germany, he added. Xi expressed China's willingness to cooperate with Germany in areas such as artificial intelligence, green and low-carbon development, trade in services and digital economy to jointly enhance future competitiveness. Both sides should support cultural, educational and artistic exchanges, facilitate personnel exchanges, foster people-to-people connectivity, and create a favorable atmosphere for celebrating the 55th anniversary of bilateral ties next year, Xi said. China has always viewed the EU as a partner, and is committed to developing China-EU relations with sincerity and goodwill, said Xi, adding that history and reality have repeatedly shown that for China and the EU, cooperation outweighs competition and consensus outweighs differences. He added that as long as both China and the EU stay committed to the positioning of their partnership and maintain the tone of equal-footed dialogue, differences and problems can be resolved and will not hinder further development of China-EU relations. It is hoped that the EU will work with China in the same direction to jointly advance an equal and orderly multipolar world and a universally beneficial and inclusive economic globalization, Xi said. Xi briefed Steinmeier on the fifth plenary session of the 20th Communist Party of China (CPC) Central Committee, adding that the CPC is willing to exchange governance experience with major political parties around the world, including those in Germany. Steinmeier, who is on a state visit to China, said that over the past 25 years, he has visited China eight times. Hailing China's rapid development, Steinmeier said China has become a major country with considerable political influence as well as economic, scientific and technological strength. Germany greatly admires the tremendous development achievements China has made under the leadership of President Xi, he noted. Germany firmly adheres to the one-China policy and is fully confident about the prospects of bilateral relations, Steinmeier said. The two countries can properly resolve economic and trade differences via dialogue and consultation to achieve win-win results, setting an example for the world, he said. Noting that the international order is under strain, and the world expects China to play a bigger role, Steinmeier said Germany is ready to jointly shoulder the responsibility of safeguarding world peace and development with China, uphold the purposes and principles of the UN Charter and the authority of international law, support free trade and WTO rules, and oppose protectionism and trade wars. Prior to the talks, Xi and his wife Peng Liyuan held a welcoming ceremony for Steinmeier and his wife Elke Büdenbender at the square outside the east entrance of the Great Hall of the People. item.title: Xi stresses Party self-governance to ensure CPC remains strong leadership core
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-30
BEIJING, Oct. 30 (Xinhua) -- Xi Jinping, general secretary of the Communist Party of China (CPC) Central Committee, stressed the need to persevere with full and rigorous Party self-governance to ensure that the CPC remains the strong leadership core in advancing socialism with Chinese characteristics. Xi made the remarks at a symposium on Aug. 21 to solicit opinions from non-Party personages on drafting the resolution of the CPC Central Committee on certain major issues concerning persevering with full and rigorous Party self-governance. The resolution was adopted at the fifth plenary session of the 20th Central Committee of the CPC, which concluded on Thursday in Beijing. Addressing the symposium, Xi said that to govern the country well, the Party must first govern itself well, and to make the country strong, the Party must first strengthen itself. Wang Huning, Cai Qi and Li Xi, who are members of the Standing Committee of the Political Bureau of the CPC Central Committee, attended the symposium. The chairpersons of the central committees of the eight non-CPC parties, the chairperson of the All-China Federation of Industry and Commerce (ACFIC) and a representative of personages without party affiliation shared their views and suggestions, and expressed full support for the draft resolution. The CPC has unswervingly promoted full and rigorous Party self-governance since its 18th National Congress in 2012, and thus grown stronger through revolutionary tempering, Xi said. At the same time, he added, profound changes in global, national and Party conditions have brought new circumstances and issues to the endeavor to advance full and rigorous Party self-governance. It is essential to build firm confidence, maintain resolve and earnestly govern the Party well and build it stronger, he said. To persevere with full and rigorous Party self-governance, it is important to make tenacious efforts to resolve prominent problems within the Party, Xi said. Efforts must be made to uphold and strengthen the CPC Central Committee's centralized, unified leadership, unwaveringly apply strict principles, improve the system of exercising full and rigorous Party self-governance, and take strengthening the Party politically as the overarching principle to advance Party building on all fronts, he said. At the symposium, Xi highlighted the need to uphold, develop and improve China's new type of political party system. He also expressed the hope that other political parties, the ACFIC and personages without party affiliation would stay committed to the original aspiration of multiparty cooperation, steadfastly uphold the leadership of the CPC, actively make proposals on state affairs, and give full play to their function of democratic oversight. ■
